Start and stop do what they say, the rainbow palette is here and editable, and dragging works where you actually press.

## 🐞 Fixed

- **Play after stop starts things again.** Stopping the queue and then pressing play on a package did nothing at all and said nothing about it: the tasks went to "queued", the instance's dispatcher turned around at its first line because the queue was still halted, and the rows just sat there. That is the whole of "it says running but nothing downloads". A start you press now releases a halt you set yourself. A pause that comes from a schedule is never overridden — the app says so instead.
- **Stop holds.** A stopped download went back to "running" about a second later, every time, because the download manager behind it kept reporting its own view of the world over the top. A state the app was told to record is now the app's to keep; only "finished" and "failed" can overrule it, because those are facts about the file rather than claims about what anybody wanted.
- **A link your filter is holding back says so.** Pressing start on one used to change nothing and give no reason. It now reports how many links a filter rule is keeping out of the queue.
- **"Follow the default instance" gives back what it took.** Turning it on discarded your own colour and corner shape; turning it off then handed you the *instance's* look instead of the one you had. A round trip through that switch quietly replaced your settings. It now puts them aside and restores them, and remembers them across a restart.
- **Dragging works where you press.** The reorder gesture only armed on the empty parts of a folder row — a long press on the caption, the start badge or the bin never reached it, and there is no way to guess that rule. A hold anywhere on the row now arms it, and the row's own buttons stop responding while the list is in reorder mode, so a hold on the bin cannot also open a delete dialog. Moving is steadier too: the gap follows the nearest row's centre rather than waiting for your finger to cross a whole card.
- **The back glyph is a triangle pointing left.** Two attempts at a proper arrow came before it, and both read as an assembly of parts at this size, because that is what they were.
- **Every glyph is the same size.** They were drawn to their own grids, so one size setting produced a viewfinder that filled its box beside a plug that filled two thirds of it — three buttons in a column wearing three visibly different icons.

## ✨ Added

- **The rainbow palette is on the settings screen**, and each of its eight colours can be edited. They belong to the instance rather than to this phone — colours are handed out by position, so a palette kept locally would make the same card teal in a browser and pink here — and editing one writes it back.
- **A colour picker**, which the app never had: a saturation/value pad, a hue rail and a hex field. It is what "the colour fields cannot be edited" was about.
- **A paste button and an ordered layout on the connection screen.** Heading, then the explanation, then the field, then the buttons.

## 🎨 Changed

- **The accent colours cannot be picked while the rainbow is on.** Worth knowing what that costs: the rainbow replaces the accent only for things that are one of a set — cards, rows, tabs. The floating action button, the primary buttons and the speed curve are one of a kind and keep the single accent, so they hold whatever was last chosen until the mode goes off again.
- **The speed graph spans the card it lives in** and is drawn inside it rather than in a box of its own. Its axis labels moved above and below the plot; a label column down the left was costing about a fifth of the width.
- GlimStone **1.7.3**.

Settings live under **Overview › the gear › Appearance**.
